title: Direct vs. Regular Mutual Funds: SEBI's New Default Plan Rule
description: Regular mutual fund plans typically include a commission for distributors, leading to higher expense ratios. Direct mutual fund plans do not involve distribut.

faq.q: What is the primary difference between direct and regular mutual funds?
faq.a: The main difference lies in the expense ratio. Regular plans include a commission for distributors, leading to a higher expense ratio, while direct plans have no distributor commission, resulting in a lower expense ratio and potentially higher returns.

faq.q: Why did SEBI introduce the new default plan rule?
faq.a: SEBI introduced this rule to promote transparency, empower investors by making them aware of lower-cost options, and encourage self-directed investing by making direct plans the default choice on online execution-only platforms.

faq.q: Will I still be able to invest in regular plans?
faq.a: Yes, you will still have the option to invest in regular plans. The new rule only mandates that direct plans be offered as the default option on execution-only platforms, but you can actively choose a regular plan if you prefer distributor services.

faq.q: How does a lower expense ratio benefit me?
faq.a: A lower expense ratio means a smaller portion of your investment is deducted annually for fund management. This leads to more units being allocated to you, which then compounds over time, potentially resulting in a significantly larger corpus in the long run.

faq.q: Can I switch my existing regular plan investments to direct plans?
faq.a: Yes, you can switch your existing regular plan investments to direct plans of the same fund. However, this process typically involves redeeming from the regular plan and reinvesting in the direct plan, which may trigger capital gains taxes and exit loads, depending on your holding period.

faq.q: Where can I find the expense ratio for a mutual fund?
faq.a: You can find the expense ratio for any mutual fund scheme on the respective Asset Management Company's (AMC) website, on the Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI) website (https://amfiindia.com), or in the scheme's offer document.
